nodes.text: Context. The IV-3 is a quadcopter used by our field teams to inspect wind-turbine blades and overhead power lines. The current battery supplier is discontinuing its product line, so a replacement pack must be selected from the shortlisted catalogue. This document lists what the replacement must, or preferably should, achieve. Requirements stated with "shall" or "must", or whose violation makes the pack unusable, are mandatory. Recommendations ("should", "preferably", "desirable", "would be appreciated") do not by themselves disqualify a candidate.

[R01] A typical inspection mission consists of 30 minutes of hovering and slow translation, during which the propulsion system and payload draw 180 W on average. The pack shall store enough energy to complete such a mission without landing. Reserve margins are handled by the flight controller and are not part of this requirement.
nodes.label: R01

nodes.text: [R02] With the payload installed, the airframe is 800 g below its maximum take-off mass. Whatever pack is chosen must not consume more than this margin.
nodes.label: R02

nodes.text: [R03] Missions are flown all year round. The pack shall deliver its rated performance at ambient temperatures from −10 °C (winter inspections) up to 45 °C (summer, in direct sun on the tarmac).
nodes.label: R03

nodes.text: [R04] Packs are shipped to field teams by air freight. A UN38.3 test summary is a precondition for the acceptance of any lithium battery by our logistics department.
nodes.label: R04

nodes.text: [R05] The electronic speed controllers and the power distribution board are rated for six lithium cells in series. Any other series configuration cannot be used.
nodes.label: R05

nodes.text: [R06] During climb and gust rejection the motors draw up to 40 A in total, sustained for more than a minute. The pack shall support this current continuously.
nodes.label: R06

nodes.text: [R07] To keep the cost of ownership acceptable, the pack should still provide 80 % of its initial capacity after at least 300 full charge–discharge cycles.
nodes.label: R07

nodes.text: [R08] The existing harness ends in an XT90 plug. Delivery with a matching connector would avoid re-soldering and is therefore preferred.
nodes.label: R08

nodes.text: [R09] Field teams carry a single charger. It is desirable that a pack can be fully recharged within 90 minutes, so that two packs can be rotated during a working day.
nodes.label: R09

nodes.text: [R10] The battery bay accepts packs up to 160 mm long; width and height are not limiting for any 6S pack in the catalogue. Longer packs cannot be mounted.
nodes.label: R10

nodes.text: [R11] A smart battery-management system that reports the state of charge to the flight controller would be appreciated.
nodes.label: R11

nodes.text: [R12] Inspections are occasionally interrupted by light rain. Preferably, the pack enclosure should be rated at least IP54.
nodes.label: R12

nodes.text: Selection. Among the candidates that satisfy every mandatory requirement, the purchasing department selects the one with the lowest unit price; if two candidates have the same price, the lighter one is chosen.
Out of scope. Charger compatibility, storage conditions and end-of-life recycling are covered by separate documents.
The Helix pack is a lithium-polymer battery built from six cells in series (6S), nominal voltage 22.2 V, rated capacity 5200 mAh.
Weight 720 g including balance lead. Dimensions 155 x 48 x 50 mm.
Discharge rating: 25C continuous, 50C burst for up to 10 s.
Recommended operating temperature: 0 °C to 50 °C. Do not charge below 5 °C.
Transport: UN38.3 test summary available on request; packs ship at 30 % state of charge.
Cycle life of at least 300 cycles to 80 % capacity at 1C/1C. Maximum charge rate 1C.
Output lead: 10 AWG silicone wire terminated with an XT60 connector.
Unit price: 189 EUR (minimum order 10 units).
Helix packs are hand-assembled in our ISO 9001 certified facility and come with a limited warranty.

nodes.evidence: Nominal voltage 22.2 V and rated capacity 5200 mAh give 22.2 x 5200 / 1000 = 115.44 Wh, which is >= 90 Wh.
Weight is 720 g including balance lead, which is <= 800 g.
Recommended operating temperature is 0 °C to 50 °C, which does not cover the required -10 °C to 45 °C range.
UN38.3 test summary is available on request, so the pack includes UN38.3 certification.
The pack is built from six cells in series (6S).
25C continuous on 5200 mAh gives 5.2 A x 25 = 130 A, which is >= 40 A.
Cycle life is at least 300 cycles to 80 % capacity, which is >= 300 cycles.
Output lead is terminated with an XT60 connector, not XT90.
The datasheet gives maximum charge rate 1C but no charge time in minutes.
Length is 155 mm, which is <= 160 mm.
The datasheet does not mention a smart BMS or SOC reporting feature.
The datasheet does not state any IP rating.

nodes.text: Nordcell N6 series pack: six lithium-ion polymer cells in series, 22.2 V nominal, 4500 mAh capacity.
Weight 640 g. Size 150 x 46 x 52 mm.
Continuous discharge 15C (67.5 A), peak 30C for 5 s.
Discharge temperature range −15 °C to 50 °C; charge between 0 °C and 40 °C.
Shipping documents: UN38.3 test summary and MSDS supplied with every order. Energy below 100 Wh, so no dangerous-goods exemption is needed for air freight.
Lifetime: 400 cycles to 80 % of initial capacity. Standard charge 1C (approximately 60 min).
Supplied with XT90 connector and 8 AWG leads. Simple protection board without communication interface.
Price: 229 EUR per unit, delivery in 3 weeks.
Nordcell is a Scandinavian start-up; all packs are designed in Gothenburg.

nodes.justification: Candidate D is the only candidate that passes all critical requirements, including R03 (operating temperature range) and R06 (continuous current), while candidates A, B, and C fail R03. Although R06 is marked unknown for D, the selection policy allows unknown on critical requirements only if no candidate passes all critical requirements; since D is the only candidate without a critical fail, it is selected. Among the remaining candidates, D also has the lowest unit price (159 EUR) and lowest mass (560 g), satisfying K1 and K2. Therefore, D is chosen based on the priority criteria.
